mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL falls monotonically from +6.0 to +3.6 across the four weekly means, showing households spending progressively less time at home; the released time converts into out-of-home discretionary trips, so RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks is higher than over the last four.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL prints 6.0, 4.7, 4.1, 3.6 across t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days while RESIDENTIAL continues to decline or stays below +4.0.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES recovers only 1.8 points over three weeks and stays near -22, so office-district daytime populations remain far below baseline; the resulting loss of commuter-linked retail footfall caps further gains, so RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks is lower than over the last four.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improves only from -23.9 to -22.1 over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES stays at or below -22.0 percent change from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL still prints above baseline at +3.6, meaning a residual stay-at-home constraint remains; once a weekly mean crosses below +3.0 that constraint is effectively released, adding a step of discretionary trips that lifts RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean crosses below +3.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at t-0w equals +3.6, one step above the +3.0 threshold
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL crosses below +3.0 and RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days is not higher than its mean over the four weeks before the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous week-on-week improvement in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals a coordinated return of commuting and station traffic; the two channels compound retail footfall exposure, producing higher RETAIL_REC over four weeks, whereas either series improving alone does not.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve at least 0.5 points week-on-week in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:in the final week WORKPLACES moves -23.3 to -22.1 while TRANSIT moves -37.6 to -37.1
failure_condition: Weeks in which WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve by 0.5 points or more are followed by RETAIL_REC means at or below the prior four-week RETAIL_REC mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS decays from +55.0 to +45.0 across the window as the outdoor-leisure season ends; once the weekly PARKS mean falls below +45.0, discretionary time shifts toward indoor commercial venues, raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean falls below +45.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS prints 55.0, 46.4, 44.3, 45.0 across t-3w to t-0w
regime_hint: seasonal transition from summer to autumn
failure_condition: After PARKS prints below +45.0, RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days does not exceed its mean over the preceding four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM makes no net progress (-16.3 to -16.1) and prints below -16.0, signalling households re-tightening toward essential-only shopping; the same caution suppresses non-essential spend, so RETAIL_REC over the next week is lower than over the last four.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM prints -16.3, -15.3, -16.0, -16.1 with no net recovery
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than its mean over the last four weeks while GROCERY_PHARM stays at or below -16.0.

mechanism_narrative: Under gradual de-escalation where TRANSIT sits within one point of its four-week high (-37.1 versus -37.6), transit-linked catch-up in shopping trips dominates and drives RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks; the channel is inactive if transit stalls or reverses.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT within 2.0 points of its trailing four-week maximum
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rises from -38.1 to -37.1 over the window, near its four-week high
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT is within 2.0 points of its trailing four-week maximum, the subsequent 14-day RETAIL_REC mean is at or below the preceding four-week RETAIL_REC mean.

mechanism_narrative: Falling PARKS visits and falling RESIDENTIAL share interact: the park decline frees discretionary hours while the residential decline pushes people out of the home, and their combination routes spending into retail, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS below +46.0 and RESIDENTIAL below +4.5 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS 55.0 to 45.0 and RESIDENTIAL 6.0 to 3.6 over the same window
failure_condition: Weeks with PARKS below +46.0 and RESIDENTIAL below +4.5 are followed by 28-day RETAIL_REC means at or below the prior four-week RETAIL_REC mean.
